stories.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
stories.body: An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Finland's President Alexander Stubb said.

stories.title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
stories.body: The truce was originally planned for the stranded residents of Oleshky, and Russia and Ukraine say no breaches have been reported.

stories.title: Mbappé sorry for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after backlash in China
stories.body: The France star had referred to the former Chinese leader as a "dictator" during an interview about memes.

stories.title: Lula's comeback in Brazil dents Trump's ambitions for Latin America
stories.body: The Trump-Lula relationship may have thawed, but several issues could reignite tensions between the two leaders.

stories.title: Dutch zookeeper dies after being mauled by leopard
stories.body: The woman began her career at the park when she was 17 and had worked there on-and-off for four decades.

stories.title: Ex-wife of Zimbabwe's vice-president freed after collapse of attempted murder case
stories.body: Marry Mubaiwa had been held on remand for seven years after being charged in 2019 for her then husband's attempted murder.

stories.title: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking case
stories.body: The three brothers were found guilty of drugging and raping several women over the course of decades.

stories.title: Egypt court fines journalist Lina Attalah and orders news site's closure
stories.body: Amnesty International said the verdict against Attalah and independent outlet Mada Masr represented "a crushing blow to press freedom".

stories.title: Ghanaian twin brothers and US woman plead guilty to $9m romance scam
stories.body: The group targeted elderly people across US and Europe, luring them into romantic relationship before persuading them to transfer large sums of money.

stories.title: Ballon d'Or ceremony raises case of French sports journalist jailed in Algeria
stories.body: He is in jail accused of supporting terrorism after travelling to the politically sensitive region Kabylie.

stories.title: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
stories.body: Overcrowding and poor ventilation caused the deaths of 33 detainees in a prison cell in Minna state.

stories.title: Controversial Islamic cleric shot dead in northern Nigeria
stories.body: Yahaya Masussuka had posted videos in which he rejected some elements of mainstream Islam.

stories.title: Jordan carries out deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for church attack
stories.body: The attack on a village in Syria killed five people, including women and children, Syrian health officials said.

stories.title: West warns of famine risk in Sudan as civil war grinds on
stories.body: Millions face acute hunger in Sudan as conflict, drought and funding cuts aggravate the humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction
stories.body: The sale of the rare skeleton reignites debate in the scientific community about whether dinosaur remains should end up in private hands or public view.

stories.title: Ex-FBI chief James Comey faces federal charges for third time
stories.body: Comey's lawyers say the case stems from alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in 2016.

stories.title: Jay-Z to perform at Super Bowl half-time show
stories.body: The rapper has been involved with the show for years but has never before performed at the NFL championship game.

stories.title: Netherlands pulls out of Eurovision again over Israel participation
stories.body: A Dutch broadcaster reverses a decision to take part, citing "sensitivities" over Israel's participation.

stories.title: Watch: 'No clear winner' in Israel election - what happens now?
stories.body: Polls have closed in the Israeli election, but there is no clear winner.

stories.title: What we know about Ukraine-Russia truce in Oleshky, brokered by Melania Trump
stories.body: The Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has had no electricity, gas or water for three years, as residents reported having to eat weeds to survive.
